picks.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
picks.why_plausible: Buys performance apparel, is brand-loyal to things that perform, and responds to technical fabrics and performance claims (price_sensitivity: low-medium). Backcountry skiing is an athletic identity purchase, exactly his mode.
picks.ad_angle: Worn by ski patrollers — the pro-grade shell that earns its keep on the skin track.

picks.name: The Wellness Optimizer
picks.why_plausible: Price_sensitivity: low and shops fitness/activewear, willing to pay premiums for products that demonstrably deliver outcomes. An outcome-focused, spec-driven pitch on a $650 shell fits her optimizer mindset.
picks.ad_angle: Spec-by-spec: why this shell keeps you dry and moving on long backcountry days — buy once, buy right.

picks.name: The Gifter
picks.why_plausible: Price_sensitivity: low, apparel affinity, and the brief flags gift as an occasion (0.5) with a high, impressive AOV. A $650 shell is a flagship gift for the skier in someone's life.
lean_into: impressive high-end gift for the skier who has everything
avoid: overly technical jargon with no payoff
picks.ad_angle: The gift a serious skier would never buy themselves — pro-level shell, season-ready shipping.

plan.summary: This catalog has no outdoor or technical-gear publisher, so the plan reduces to a single activewear test on Movewell, with Cloudfoot as the best male-skewing backup if that underdelivers.

test.name: Movewell
test.rationale: Movewell's "Fitness-engaged shoppers" at 25-44 with mid-high income are the closest thing in this catalog to an active, gear-buying audience, and 22M impressions gives a $650 shell enough volume to find its few qualified buyers. The 82% female, studio-fitness skew is a long way from backcountry touring, so treat it as a prospecting test, not a core placement.
test.risk: $700 against a $78 typical order is a 9x ask, and an activewear publisher may view technical outerwear as adjacent competition.

test.name: Cloudfoot
test.adjustment_reason: Notes show a near-even gender split (47% male) and 25-45 age band matching the brief's audience, plus 'activewear' and 'sustainable' subcategories — a better outdoor-adjacent read than the 36 category score suggests.
test.rationale: Cloudfoot is the only balanced-gender activewear publisher here, with "Tech-adjacent urban professionals" at a $118 AOV — the least painful price gap among apparel options. Still excluded on fit, but it's the first place to look if the Movewell test underdelivers on male reach.

evidence.quote: Tech-adjacent urban professionals. Comfort + sustainability messaging

test.risk: Comfort and sustainability messaging is a poor match for a performance-only brand that leads with ski patrollers.

campaign.name: Technical ski shells and outerwear for backcountry skiing · post-purchase launch

bid_strategy.rationale: $700 first order × 0.30 = $210.00 target CPA: one-time purchase, so the first order has to pay back the acquisition. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: Assumed the product is sold to both men and women since the brief doesn't say.
Assumed a typical first order of about $700 based on the $650 starting price.
Assumed a one-time purchase, not a subscription.
Allowable CPA is 30% of first order value (one time); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: No publisher cleared the recommended bar, so the whole budget is a test. Treat results as exploratory.
